quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Datroway approved in the EU as only TROP2-directed medicine (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Datroway (datopotamab deruxtecan) as monotherapy for the 1st-line treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) who are not candidates for PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor therapy, following the positive CHMP opinion; Datroway is now approved for two breast cancer indications in the EU. The approval is based on the TROPION-Breast02 Phase III trial (644 patients): median overall survival 23.7 months versus 18.7 months with chemotherapy (a 5.0-month improvement; HR 0.79), a 43% reduction in the risk of disease progression or death (HR 0.57), and an objective response rate of 62.5% versus 29.3%. Datroway was approved in the US in May 2026 for the same indication; reviews are underway in China and Japan, and in Australia, Canada, Singapore and Switzerland under Project Orbis. It is approved in more than 30 countries/regions for this TNBC indication and in more than 45 for HR-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. EVP Dave Fredrickson: more than 80,000 people in Europe are diagnosed with TNBC every year. Daiichi Sankyo's Ken Keller: Datroway is the only TROP2-directed ADC approved in the EU with an overall survival benefit in 1st-line metastatic TNBC (company claim).
